dataset.name: SPRUCE Pretreatment Plant Tissue Analyses, 2009 through 2013
description: This data set reports the results of elemental analyses of foliar and stem/woody twig plant tissues collected at the SPRUCE site in 2009, 2012, and 2013. Samples were obtained at various locations around the S1 Bog and from within the developing experimental treatment plots. These are pretreatment vegetation samples, collected prior to initiation of the SPRUCE experiment heating and elevated CO2 treatments. The experimental work was conducted in a Picea mariana [black spruce] - Sphagnum spp. bog forest in northern Minnesota, 40 km north of Grand Rapids, in the USDA Forest Service Marcell Experimental Forest (MEF).

measurementTechnique:
Site Description:
The site is the 8.1-ha S1 bog, a Picea mariana [black spruce] – Sphagnum spp. ombrotrophic bog forest in northern Minnesota, 40 km north of Grand Rapids, in the USDA Forest Service Marcell Experimental Forest (MEF). The S1 bog was harvested in successive strip cuts in 1969 and 1974 and the cut areas were allowed to naturally regenerate. The 1974 strips are characterized by medium density of 3-5 meter black spruce and larch trees with an open canopy. The 1969 harvest strips are characterized by a higher density of 3-5 meter black spruce and larch trees with a generally closed canopy.

Sampling Design:
In 2009, selected species (Ledum (Rhododendron), Spruce) were surveyed across the entire bog at pre-treatment survey plot locations, avoiding edges and lag areas. During that survey, current year needles or leaves were collected from five individual plants per species, and then pooled for analysis.
In 2012 and 2013, vegetation samples were collected from plots 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, and 21. A ¼ meter square sampling frame was place within a hummock and a hollow location within each plot. All plant material excluding the sphagnum was cut from the squares and bagged for analysis. Plots 1, 3, 12, and 18 were not sampled.

Plant Tissue Processing:
After collection, samples were kept on blue ice and transported to the SPRUCE office in Grand Rapids, MN for initial sorting and drying prior to shipment to ORNL for analysis (clipped plots), or shipped directly on blue ice to ORNL for processing and analysis (survey plots). Samples were sorted by species, dried at 70 °C, weighed, and ground. These samples were then used to assess leaf area index (and stem area index for clipped plots), and analyzed for a suite of macro- and micro- nutrients.
Analytical Methods:
ORNL
CN Analyses (Brice and Phillips) – The samples were oven-dried at 70°C and ground to a fine powder. Approximately 0.1 g of ground sample was analyzed for carbon and nitrogen on a LECO TruSpec elemental analyzer (LECO Corporation, St. Joseph, MI). Duplicate samples and a standard of known carbon and nitrogen concentration (alfalfa lot 1015, LECO Corporation, carbon = 45.17 % ± 0.31 % SD, nitrogen = 3.32 % ± 0.04 % SD) were used to ensure the accuracy and precision of the data.
Phosphorus (Childs) – For the 2009 whole bog survey, total phosphorus analysis was conducted on 0.2 g of dried foliar tissue that was digested with sulfuric acid in a Lachat BD40 block digestor at 390 degrees C for 3 hours, then assessed using a Lachat Quick-Chem 8500 Flow Injection Analysis System, method 13-115-01-1-B, “Total Phosphorus in Kjedahl Digests.”
University of Georgia
Total Element Analyses (Brice and Phillips) – Total element analysis was conducted on 1 gram of dried and homogenized bulk material for the assessment of P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Mn, Fe, Al, B, Cu, Zn, Na, Ni, Pb, Cr. The method employed was HNO3 microwave digestion followed by inductively coupled plasma spectroscopy. Analyses were conducted on a Thermo Jarrell-Ash model 61E ICP (EPA 3051; 200.7) at the University of Georgia.
